chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Al-Husayn ibn Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And remember your Lord when you forget' [18:24]. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When you swear an oath and forget to make an exception (by saying 'If Allah wills'), then make the exception when you remember.'

key_terms.تَسْتَثْنِيَ: To make an exception (specifically referring to saying 'Insha'Allah')

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets to say 'If Allah wills' while making an oath?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the Quranic command to 'remember your Lord when you forget' specifically applies to the omission of 'Insha'Allah' in oaths. This establishes the juristic principle that forgetting the condition does not invalidate the oath, but rather requires its immediate recitation upon remembrance to align with divine will. This interpretation underscores the Shia emphasis on ease in religious obligations and the continuous awareness of God's sovereignty in human speech.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hassan, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Al Husayn Bin Zurara who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [18:24] and remember your Lord when you forget. So heasws said: ‘When you swear an oath and forget to say the exclusion (إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ), so say the exclusion when you remember’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hassan from Ali ibn Asbat from al-Husayn ibn Zurarah who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘. . . speak of your Lord if you forget.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘It is when you take an oath and forget to make the exception (saying if Allah so wills), then you must make the exception when you remember.’”
